newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela Viasa may file bankruptcy within 2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela Viasa may file bankruptcy within 2 weeks.

text.p: Troubled Venezuelan airline Viasa may file for bankruptcy within the next two weeks if shareholders fail to reach an agreement with Spanish airline Iberia at a scheduled Thursday meeting, a leading daily El Nacional reported.
"Viasa's problems don't have much hope of being solved," said Venezuelan Investment Fund (FIV) president Alberto Poletto, El Nacional reported.

"The only way out looks like bankruptcy, unless a new partner is found," Poletto said. Poletto said shareholders could file for bankruptcy under Venezuelan commercial law. Viasa was not immediately available for comment.
Venezuela's government, a 40 percent shareholder in the airline, has refused to pump more money in the carrier.

Iberia, which has a 45 percent share, meanwhile says it has already injected $272 million into the airline and cannot stump up more under European Union directives. Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial holds the remaining 15 percent share.

Viasa workers, who say the company's problems stem from poor management by Iberia, rejected a restructuring proposal by the national Spanish carrier earlier this month that would have cut routes and slashed payrolls.
In an alternative bid to save the company, they have contracted French investment house Banque Paribas to seek-out possible new partners.
Laden with $147 million in debts with Iberia, the airline lost $30 million last year.
